# Role Prep docs standard

`docs/` holds the decisions behind Role Prep: why it exists, who it serves,
what we build, how it looks and how the repo works. Content for learners lives in `content/roleprep/`, never here.

## Folder and order

Docs are numbered in reading order. Each one builds on the ones before it,
so a newcomer can read top to bottom and never meet a term before it is
explained.

| File | Answers | Depends on |
|---|---|---|
| `README.md` | What is here and in what order to read it | all |
| `01-business-case.md` | Why build it, for whom, why we win | — |
| `02-use-cases.md` | Who uses it, for what, and the journey they take | 01 |
| `03-epic-features-stories.md` | What we build, in which phase, with acceptance criteria | 01, 02 |
| `04-ux-ui-plan.md` | How every feature looks and behaves | 02, 03 |
| `05-repo-brand-agent-kit-plan.md` | Where the code, content and agents live and how they work | 03, 04 |

A new doc takes the next free number, or slots in by renumbering when it
must be read earlier. Renumbering means updating every link to it, the
README and `docs.order` in `kit.json` in the same change.

File names: `NN-kebab-case.md`. Only `README.md` is unnumbered.

## Every doc's shape

```markdown
# <Title in sentence case>

> <One sentence: what this doc decides and who it is for.>
>
> Status: Draft | Approved · Updated: YYYY-MM-DD · Owner: Ajeet Chouksey
> Reads after: [01 …](01-….md) · Next: [03 …](03-….md)

## <Sections…>
```

- One `#` heading per file. Sections are `##`, sub-sections `###`. Never skip a level.
- Sentence-case headings. No numbering inside headings; the file name carries the order.
- The first doc has no "Reads after"; the last has no "Next".
- Owner is a person's name, never an @-handle.
- Dates are absolute (`2026-11-03`), never "today" or "last week".

## Writing

- Lead each section with its conclusion, then the evidence.
- Tables for comparisons, numbered lists for steps, prose for reasoning.
- Numbers, prices, market sizes and names come from the source and keep it.
  Mark an estimate as an estimate. Never round a figure into a stronger claim.
- Use the vertical's own vocabulary as its content-standard skill defines it.
- No marketing filler ("revolutionary", "seamless", "unlock").

## Links

- Between docs: relative links, with anchors where useful, `(04-ux-ui-plan.md#key-flows)`.
- To repo files: relative from `docs/`, `[validator](../scripts/check-docs.mjs)`.
- To prototypes and visual artifacts: full `https://claude.ai/artifact/…` URL with a
  sentence saying what the reader will see there.
- Every link must resolve. `check-docs.mjs` fails on a broken file or anchor link.

## Diagrams

Diagrams are rich, professional SVGs in AaryaAI brand v2, never Mermaid.
Follow `svg-diagram-craft` for when a diagram earns its place, the design
system and the build loop. In short:

1. **Source and output.** Each diagram is `docs/diagrams/src/<NN-name>.mjs`
   built with `scripts/diagram-kit.mjs`; `npm run diagrams` writes
   `docs/diagrams/<NN-name>.svg`. `NN` is the number of the doc it belongs to.
2. **Embed.** `![<one-sentence alt text>](diagrams/<NN-name>.svg)` on its own
   line, then a plain italic caption line directly under it stating the
   diagram's claim in 5–12 words.
3. **Look before you ship.** Preview light and dark PNGs and fix every overlap
   or cramped label before the doc is done.

No Mermaid blocks, raw HTML, screenshots of diagrams, or exported widget
placeholders (`[embedded content: …]`). When importing a doc whose diagram was
dropped, redraw it from the widget's own code where available, else from the
surrounding text, with the same parts, connections and claim.

## Importing from Claude Docs or artifacts

1. Export the doc as Markdown and decode the base64 to a scratch file with
   Node. Never transcribe base64 by eye; if the export can't be saved, read
   the source as text.
2. Keep every section, table, number and decision. Restructure only to fit
   the shape above.
3. Turn chips into text: a date chip becomes the `Updated:` date, a person
   chip becomes the owner name.
4. Replace every dropped widget with an SVG diagram, per the rules above.
5. Add a `Source:` line at the end with the original doc's link. The repo copy
   is the source of truth from then on.

## Checks

`scripts/check-docs.mjs` runs after every write under `docs/` via the
PostToolUse hook, and in CI. It fails on:

- a file name that is not `README.md` or `NN-kebab-case.md`;
- zero or more than one `#` heading, or a skipped heading level;
- a numbered doc missing from `README.md`;
- a relative link to a missing file or heading;
- an exported placeholder (`embedded content`, `&#91;`) left in;
- any Mermaid block;
- a diagram image without alt text or without an italic caption under it;
- an SVG in `docs/diagrams/` with no source in `docs/diagrams/src/`, no
  `<title>`/`<desc>`/`viewBox`, a script, `foreignObject` or external
  reference, or that no doc embeds.

`scripts/build-diagrams.mjs --check` fails CI when an SVG is stale against its source.
